title: Grateful Dead Live at William and Mary College Hall on 1973-09-11
lineage: aud>?>7" reel @ 3.75 ips, no nr technics rs-1506>hd-p2 24/96>cd wave>adobe audition 2.0>flac; transferred/seeded by Rob Berger

ai_review.summary: Muffled audience tape captures a solid early‑70s set highlighted by a spectacular Weather Report Suite > Let It Grow and a tasty Dark Star, despite some sound cuts.
ai_review.review: The performance is strong throughout, with the Weather Report Suite into Let It Grow standing out as a showcase of the band’s tight interplay and Jerry Garcia’s ever‑changing guitar tones. Highlights also include a focused Dark Star, playful “Let Me Sing Your Blues Away,” and solid renditions of China>Rider and Playin’. The audience recording is noticeably muffled in places and suffers from a chopped Dew segment, but it remains listenable for fans who appreciate pre‑78 AUDs.

ai_rating.rationale: Show quality is consistently praised with several standout songs; recording quality is acceptable but has muffling and a major cut, yielding an overall rating just below four stars.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Muffled sound and occasional lack of clarity; decent overall balance for an audience tape but includes noticeable dropout/chopped Dew segment and audible crowd chatter.

standout_songs: Weather Report Suite > Let It Grow
Let Me Sing Your Blues Away
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set laid‑back with solid transitions; second set features rare horn accompaniment and a seamless Weather Report Suite into Let It Grow, giving the concert a cohesive yet exploratory feel.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for varied, tasteful guitar tones and a ‘seminar‑like’ performance; responsive in Dark Star.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for leading sections of Dark Star and his characteristic grumpiness with photographers; solid bass foundation.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s vocals on “Let Me Sing Your Blues Away” are highlighted as interesting; keyboards blend well with the horn section.
